subject: Post-call: Ops & unit-econ recap — model mix and target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-analytics.com>, Kevin Ross <kevin.ross@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Ops & unit-econ recap — model mix and target $/1M tokens

Hi Alice / Kevin —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks to size a realistic pilot:

1) Workloads you called out 
   - Chat-based customer triage (short-turnaround, 1–2 prompts per session; high concurrency)
   - Retrospective document embedding + semantic search for analytics queries
   - Reranking layer for top-10 search results on heavy queries (~10% of chat traffic)

2) Clarify volumes we estimated on the call (please confirm):
   - Expected daily active sessions: 6k – 12k (peak concurrency ~600)
   - Avg tokens per chat session (input+output): 1.2k tokens
   - Monthly token estimate (conservative): 1.6M — aggressive: 5.6M

3) Target unit economics you mentioned: you want to cap inference at roughly $800–$1,400 per 1M tokens during pilot. We flagged a few levers to hit that (model mix, quantized model variants, and batching).

4) Proposed model split for pilot (starter suggestion):
   - Chat generation: 70% of tokens — use a cost-balanced chat model (gpt-style open variant)
   - Embeddings: 20% — high-precision small embedding model for vector DB updates
   - Rerank: 10% — dedicated rerank model called only on top-N

Next steps / asks:
- Alice: can you confirm the monthly token target you want us to price to (pick one: 2M / 4M / 6M)?
- Kevin: can you share any regulatory constraints around token persistence or KMS?
- Lauren & Ben: I asked to prep a price-scenario sheet with $/1M targets at different model-weightings — sending v2 shortly.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios, model mappings)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if that's easier.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops & unit-econ recap — model mix and target $/1M tokens

Mateo —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Monthly target: let's plan to price to a 4M tokens/month pilot (we can ramp to 6M if the SLA & throughput look good).
- Token mix: we expect chat to dominate (~65% tokens), embeddings ~25% (we do nightly bulk updates), rerank ~10%. Your initial split maps closely to ours.
- Unit-econ target: the $800–$1,400 /1M target was approximate. Steering committee wants an illustrative option at $1,000/1M as a baseline and a stretch at $800/1M.
- Security: we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys and a short retention profile for raw prompts (30 days). SOC2 evidence will be required for procurement — we can share the questionnaire next week.

Could you also annotate the pricing sheet with two rows: (A) baseline model family (higher quality) and (B) quantized variants (lower $/token) so we can see tradeoffs?

We are available for a 20-minute follow-up on Thursday 7/17 at 10:00am PT if that works.

Best,
Alice Gomez
Head of Product Ops, Acme Analytics
alice.gomez@acme-analytics.com | +1 (212) 555-0187

Subject: Pricing scenarios & model-weighting options (attached)

Hi Alice / Kevin —

Following Mateo's note, attached is a quick scenarios export (rows summarized):

Scenario 1 — Baseline quality
   - Model: ChatLarge-v1 (float16)
   - Expected $/1M: $1,200
   - Notes: best quality; higher latency at peak

Scenario 2 — Quantized blend
   - Model: ChatLarge-q4_1 + ChatMedium-q4_0 (cache-aware routing)
   - Expected $/1M: $880
   - Notes: ~10% quality delta on edge cases; ~30% cost savings

Scenario 3 — Aggressive cost-first
   - Model: ChatMedium-q4_0 for most traffic + offload long-context to batch jobs
   - Expected $/1M: $650
   - Notes: slight increase in tokenization noise; best unit econ

Model-split variants included in the sheet — you can toggle the % share per line to see blended $/1M. Link to live sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme

Attachments: redwood_pricing_v2.xlsx, acme_discovery-notes.pdf

Next step: if 1k/1M is the baseline you want to present, I recommend Scenario 2 (quantized blend) as the starting price for procurement conversations; Scenario 1 as a premium option.

I'll plan to join the Thursday 7/17 10:00am PT call; Mateo can send calendar invite.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
